title: Add validation and documentation to preprocessing utilities
body:
Summary

This PR improves the robustness and documentation of the preprocessing utilities used for LIVECell inference.

Changes

* Added docstrings to the preprocessing function.
* Added validation for empty input images.
* Added validation for non-positive magnification downsample factors.
* Added a safeguard against invalid median intensity values during image normalization.

Motivation

These changes improve error reporting and prevent runtime failures caused by invalid inputs while preserving the existing preprocessing behavior for valid images.

title: Do any models trained on LIVECell inherit the non-commercial restriction?
body:
Hi,

This dataset looks great!

I see it has a license statement:

> All images, annotations and models associated with LIVECell are published under Attribution-NonCommercial 4.0 International ([CC BY-NC 4.0](https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-nc/4.0/)) license.

My question is: **what does this mean for any models *other people* might train using LIVECell?**

I ask because we have* developed an open-source cell segmentation method, [InstanSeg](https://forum.image.sc/t/announcing-instanseg-a-new-nucleus-and-cell-segmentation-tool/101599).

We are releasing several pre-trained models to the community.  We would like to make these freely-available under open-source licenses where possible (e.g. Apache v2.0).

Because 'non-commercial' isn't compatible with [the Open Source Definition](https://opensource.org/osd), we are not sure under what license terms (if any) we are able to share any models trained on LIVECell. We'd rather not add a non-commercial restriction to our models if it isn't necessary, because this quickly becomes complex - even for academic, open-source projects like ours (e.g. see https://freedomdefined.org/Licenses/NC).

Thanks,

Pete

*-Well, more accurately '@ThibautGoldsborough has'

title: Multiple/overlapping cell annotations
body:
Hi! Thank you very much for making this dataset publicly available! 
I am not familiar with microscope images and I am new in dealing with cell segmentations. title: Training vs. Validation loss, as reported in the article
body:
Hello everyone,

First, thanks for releasing such an amazing dataset! Incredible work!

I’m currently training a model on your dataset for my engineering degree, and was wondering how you generate with Detectron2 the validation loss, as reported in the supplementary notes:
   "All training was run for a predefined set of iterations and the loss on a
    validation set, separate from the training and test sets, were monitored to assess model over- and under-fitting. Model checkpoints 
    were saved and used for evaluation based on which had the lowest validation loss (Supplementary Figs. 9 and 10) on the rationale 
    that the lowest validation loss represents a good balance between an under- and over-fitted model."

```
d = dataset_dicts[300] # choosing a random image
img = cv2.imread(d["file_name"])
outputs = predictor(img)
instances = outputs['instances']
v = Visualizer(img[:, :, ::-1],
                   scale=1, 
                   instance_mode=ColorMode.IMAGE_BW   # remove the colors of unsegmented pixels
    )
v = v.draw_instance_predictions(instances.to("cpu"))
cv2_imshow(v.get_image()[:, :, ::-1])
```

![pred_image300](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/18211142/140103586-ec1b4c4a-4ea7-4f43-a0bf-7628af61ab10.png)

It detected something, but they have a very odd shape, and the object labels are also not "cell" in the output image.

Do you have a quick solution to fix this issue?

title: Annotation missing for an image?
body:
Hi, 

First, thanks a lot for releasing this amazing resource of cell annotations! 

After downloading the data via `aws s3 sync s3://livecell-dataset .` I noticed that the training image `MCF7_Phase_E4_1_00d00h00m_1.tif` seems to have no corresponding annotation mask:

```
cd LIVECell_dataset_2021/

fname=MCF7_Phase_E4_1_00d00h00m_1.tif

find images/ -name $fname
# images/livecell_train_val_images/MCF7/MCF7_Phase_E4_1_00d00h00m_1.tif

grep -o $fname annotations/LIVECell/*json
# <no output>
``` 

compared to e.g. `MCF7_Phase_F4_1_00d00h00m_1.tif`

```
fname=MCF7_Phase_F4_1_00d00h00m_1.tif

find images/ -name $fname
# images/livecell_train_val_images/MCF7/MCF7_Phase_F4_1_00d00h00m_1.tif

grep -o $fname annotations/LIVECell/*json
# annotations/LIVECell/livecell_coco_train.json:MCF7_Phase_F4_1_00d00h00m_1.tif

```
